title: I Let the Taxi Meter Catch the Scenic Route They Swore Was Faster

parts.text: I sat in the back at 6:18 p.m. from downtown to the airport and watched the driver ignore the GPS for a scenic parkway. He said it was faster. The meter disagreed in real time. I was thirty-six, flight at 8:10, holding a phone with the city's posted shortest-path rule. I asked him to stop, showed the rule, and asked for a reprint at the curb using the meter button that prints disputes. He cursed. He printed. The airport taxi booth took the slip and adjusted down to the GPS estimate. I made the flight. Scenic is for Sundays. Meters are for Tuesdays. I tipped on the adjusted fare because the booth, not the parkway, had done work. The phone went to airplane mode over a city that still has a button.

social.video_title: The dispute button knew the parkway — Part 1/1
social.description: 8:10 flight, faster scenic, city shortest-path rule. Booth adjusted. Have you watched a meter lie with a smile?
